1.1: 1.1 Argument. Simon Peter declares that the wise of this world are dead by faith, and makes manifest to them, clearer than the light itself, how great is the greatness of piety. Simon. BEDE. He writes this to the same to whom he wrote the first epistle, etc., down to they have not yielded, let them not yield to heretics. Servant and Apostle. The person of the writer is commended. Equal. BEDE. He recognizes them as equals to himself, not because of circumcision, but because they had received the same grace and faith of Christ which they themselves had, and exercised it by works. In righteousness. This righteousness human prudence did not discover, nor did the institution of the law teach, but our Savior showed it in the Gospel: Unless your righteousness abound more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven, Matthew 5.
1.2: 1.2 Grace to you. BEDE. In the first Epistle he wrote be multiplied; in this, be fulfilled: because that he writes to beginners, this to the more perfect. Grace is multiplied in those who make good progress in this life through faith, it will be fulfilled in those who arrive in the other life through sight. Hence he adds, in the knowledge of God, that is that you may know the one true God, and him whom he sent, Jesus Christ.
1.3: 1.3 As all things. THE SAME. So may the grace of Christ be fulfilled, etc., down to but weak and inglorious he restored by his power and glory.
1.4: 1.4 He has given us the greatest and precious promises. That is eternal life which we obtain through knowledge of him. Or the things he promised us, about the conversion of others through us, or about the coming of the Holy Spirit, or about the power of miracles he has given.
1.5: 1.5 Supply in your faith. BEDE. Not only flee the concupiscence of the world, etc., down to that you be not soft and dissolute.
1.6: 1.6 And in knowledge, abstinence. THE SAME. When you have learned to do good, in the hope of eternal life abstain at once from evils, both in thought and in work, lest the knowledge of heavenly things fall to nothing if anyone does not restrain himself from the allurements of the world.
1.7: 1.7 And in godliness. THE SAME. Do not, with an eye to anything else, bestow works of piety on your adversaries, except of brotherly love, that you may pray for them that they be converted, who by your teaching or rebukes are unwilling to be converted.
1.8: 1.8 For if these be with you, etc. Therefore hold these and minister them to others, because if all these be with you in affection of heart, and even abound, that is prevail against the wars of the vices, they will not make you empty of virtues in this world, or without fruit in the future.
1.9: 1.9 Blind and groping by hand. BEDE. The eye signifies knowledge, the hand operation, etc., down to he could not foreknow, he falls into. Receiving forgetfulness. When a man falls from sin to sin, he seems to have forgotten the pact which he made with God in baptism.
1.10: 1.10 You shall never sin. That is, you will attain to eternal life, where you will sin no more. Or you will avoid mortal sins, which he who commits will not have inheritance in the kingdom of Christ, from which he remains free, the Lord helping, who has devoted himself to the aforesaid virtues. But without venial sins no one can be.
1.11: 1.11 For so. BEDE. Ezekiel speaking of the building set on the mountain, etc., down to and the God of gods shall be seen in Zion, Psalm 83.
1.12: 1.12 I will begin always to put you in remembrance of these things. That you may have an open entrance to the Holy of Holies, again and again I will admonish you, and I will always be at the beginning, because there will never be an end of admonition. What therefore is not irksome to me to repeat often, let it not be burdensome to you to hear often. And indeed knowing. BEDE. Why does he wish to admonish those who know and are established? That, namely, they may exercise in works the knowledge they have, and keep with fixed mind the truth in whose presence they are established, lest at some time through masters of error they fall from the simplicity and chastity of the faith.
1.13: 1.13 And I think it just, etc. Therefore I will admonish, because I think it just, for the reason that the Lord kindly called me, and confirmed me, and bade me confirm others, saying: Confirm your brethren, to stir you up as sleepers to these aforesaid things, being always solicitous in admonishing.
1.14: 1.14 The putting off of my tabernacle. BEDE. Beautifully he calls it not death but putting off, because for the servants of God to pluck out the bonds of the flesh is as for travelers, the journey completed, to go to their own house instead of the dwelling of a tent, as for those on an expedition, the enemy laid low, to return to their country.
1.15: 1.15 And I will endeavor. Because I shall soon pass, therefore meanwhile while I live, I will endeavor that you may frequently, namely as often as the false teachers press and wish to draw you away, have these things in memory after my departure, when you will not have me present as teacher, not to have them in any way, but so that you make a memory of them by fulfilling in work, and by teaching others. After my departure, etc. Departure is said of the saints when they go out to meet the Bridegroom.
1.16: 1.16 For we have not followed cunningly devised fables, etc. BEDE. Here he touches both pagans and heretics. The pagans did not fear to call gods whatever delighted them. The heretics, having received the mysteries of the true God, for the rest did not attend to the divine Scriptures but rather strove to transfer them to an erroneous sense by interpreting them badly. But made eyewitnesses, etc. The transfiguration of the Lord and his brightness was a sign of his resurrection and ours. By Elijah who appeared with him is understood the resurrection of those who were before the law. By Moses, of those under the law; by Peter, James and John, of those under grace. Or, by Moses dead, of the dead, by the living, of the living.
1.19: 1.19 And we have the more firm. What I have told you is not fabulous, but certain, and not only declared by these signs, but also for the confirmation of our preaching we have the prophetic word of David: The Lord said to me, You are my Son, Psalm 2, etc., more firm among other prophets, because he prophesied more clearly than others about Christ. To which you do well to attend. BEDE. That you may be able to have the light of knowledge, etc., down to in comparison with the life to come we need a lamp.
1.20: 1.20 Understanding this first. Attend to the prophetic word, for it is from God. Which can be proved by this, that prophecy is not written in such words and in such a manner of speech as men use in their speaking, and as secular writings are composed and interpreted. And truly the speech of the prophets is not according to their own will, or that of the hearers, but according to the will of the Holy Spirit who spoke in them.
1.21: 1.21 For prophecy came not by the will of man. BEDE. As it was not in the power of the prophets always to have the spirit, always to foretell the future: so it was not in their power to teach whatever they wished, but they said only what they had learned from the Spirit. These things are said lest anyone expound the Scriptures at his own pleasure.
2.1: 2.1 Destruction. Deservedly they bring destruction on themselves who deny their Redeemer, or preach him not such as the truth shows but such as they themselves feign. And therefore, alien from the Redeemer, they expect nothing more certain than the pit.
2.2: 2.2 The way of truth shall be blasphemed. BEDE. Through heretics, not only in those whom they associate to their heresy, seduced, but also in those whom they stir up to hatred of the Christian name by their most impure deeds and the sacrifices or execrable mysteries they perform, the unskilled thinking all Christians given to such crimes, the way of truth is wont to be blasphemed.
2.4: 2.4 For if God did not spare the angels. THE SAME. If God handed over the apostate angels to the pains of hell, etc., down to were snatched into the depths of the abyss.
2.5: 2.5 The original world. THE SAME. It is the same world after the flood as before, etc., down to the just will receive the glory of life.
2.6: 2.6 And the cities. These cities were reduced to fire in two ways, because first he reduced them by fire to ashes with the adjacent lands, and when afterwards the Dead Sea's waves covered the places of the fire, he willed the surrounding region still to keep the likeness of the ancient punishment. For apples most beautiful grow, which stir the desire of eating in the beholders. If you pluck them, they crumble and dissolve into ashes, and raise smoke as if still burning. Into ashes. The fire which once punished the Sodomites signifies that the impious are to suffer without end. That the land smokes, that the most beautiful fruits have ashes and stench within, hints that carnal love, though it smiles on fools, yet reserves nothing in invisible things but a fire for them, or that the smoke of their torments may rise to them forever and ever.
2.7: 2.7 Lot oppressed. BEDE. The unjust deeds and words of his neighbors tormented the just man, which, seeing, he could not correct, but he himself kept himself in good acts. He did not darken himself with the shameful things seen or heard. He is also called just in seeing and hearing; because they saw nothing in him, heard nothing about him, except what pertained to righteousness.
2.9: 2.9 The unjust. The false teachers and their followers, and therefore do not follow them. Unto the day of judgment. BEDE. Even before the day of judgment, released from the body they suffer punishments, and in the judgment they await heavier, when they will be tormented in body and soul.
2.11: 2.11 Where angels. There the unjust will be tormented where the evil angels, who before had been proud against God, and were punished for it, now do not carry but rather cast away the judgment of pride against God: which is execrable against themselves, because they are gravely punished for it, and, terrified by the greatness of the punishments, now desist from presumption of that judgment: but these unjust do not yet desist. Or they will be tormented there, that is with God: where the angels, not good, do not endure, but avenge if anything execrable is said against them.
2.13: 2.13 The reward of injustice. BEDE. That is, punishment for evil works, and especially for those who, serving corruption of the flesh and held by mad errors, blaspheme the conduct of the just, and do not cease to detract from those who think soundly.
2.17: 2.17 These are. The false apostles are not to be imitated, because though they seem useful, there is nothing in them but vanity and uncleanness.
2.18: 2.18 Proud things. Proudly saying they are just, though it is vain, desiring carnally and living luxuriously they allure those who have for a little while escaped from sins; who though they are like them, nevertheless to some extent decline their company, and abstain somewhat from sins. In the desires of the flesh, etc. Unclean is everyone who exalts his heart, that those who have for a little escaped from sins may return to their error and strive in luxury.
2.20: 2.20 For if, etc., by the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, etc. If, fleeing the pollution both of soul and of body which the world sends in, they are again entangled (as before baptism) and overcome by those pollutions, it appears that their latter state is worse than the former: because they offend God more than before baptism, and will suffer greater punishments, because the promises made in baptism are lies.
2.22: 2.22 For it has happened to them. BEDE. In Proverbs it is set down with explanation, etc., down to before the eyes of God it makes even tears themselves filthy.
3.1: 3.1 This second epistle, behold, to you. As if he said: I have already written another Epistle to repel the false teachers; and to show you my great solicitude, behold for the same cause I write also this second Epistle.
3.2: 3.2 That you may be mindful. That is, that through those Epistles you may be mindful of those words which I myself being present foretold to you. Of the words, I say, received from the holy prophets, which are confirmed by the authority of the holy prophets, and may be mindful of the precepts of the holy apostles: lest you let go the precepts which the holy apostles gave you, for the preaching of those false teachers, and which precepts are also of the Lord and Savior, because the Lord himself, who came to save us, established these precepts and commanded them to be kept.
3.5: 3.5 It escapes them. BEDE. Therefore they say all things continue in the same manner, etc., down to unto the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men.
3.8: 3.8 But of this one thing. Having proved that the judgment will truly be, he shows how effective the future is. If it is said to you by false teachers: You can do what you will, because so much time remains until the day of judgment, that the judge from the length of time will not be able to know many things; do not believe them, because whatever can be done in a thousand years, he sees as he does that which is done in one day. If they say: In a thousand years, by repenting you will not obtain pardon of offenses; do not believe: because one day of true repentance avails as much for salvation as a thousand years, as with the thief. As a thousand years. BEDE. In the acknowledgment of divine power, etc., down to whence it is rightly added:
3.9: 3.9 The Lord is not slack. And because he sees all things, you can believe that the Lord is not slack in fulfilling promises, because the time has not yet come when he will fulfill what is to be fulfilled. But therefore he delays, that he may first fulfill the sum of the elect which he foresaw, whence in the Apocalypse: And it was said to them that they should rest yet a little time, till their fellow servants be filled up, Apocalypse 6.
3.10: 3.10 The heavens with a great noise. The heavens, that is the saints; if therefore there is anything in them to be purged, it will be purged by fire. The elements. BEDE. The four by which the world consists, etc., down to and through temporal punishment, will be dissolved for the better.
3.13: 3.13 But new heavens. THE SAME. He does not say, others, but the old and ancient to be changed for the better, etc., down to we have also in the prophets: The light of the lamp shall shine there no more, Isaiah 65.
3.14: 3.14 Be diligent to be found unspotted and blameless. These are the watches of which it is said: Blessed are those servants whom the Lord when he comes shall find watching. He watches who keeps himself free from filth, who as far as in him lies has peace with all men, who subjects all the allurements of the flesh to the rule of the spirit, enjoying in himself a most happy peace.
3.15: 3.15 Our brother. BEDE. He says Paul wrote to them, in which he shows, etc., down to and through these they may stir themselves to progress.
3.16: 3.16 Hard things. In the Epistles of Paul which are depraved by heretics, etc., down to some loosening the reins of luxury, and many other things, etc. They wrest. BEDE. There is no book of the Old or New Testament in which heretics have not perverted something, either by taking away, or adding, or changing. The only remedy for the unlearned is to give hearing with humble steadiness to the words of the teachers, which steadiness since the heretics do not have, they are carried off from the Church like light chaff by the wind of pride, to their own perdition.
